title: ContextSafe FHIR R4 JSON source profile 0.1
description: The exact subset of a FHIR R4 JSON document that `contextsafe import --format fhir-r4-json` reads: one Patient, alone or as the only entry of a Bundle, carrying synthetic identifiers, synthetic HumanName tokens, and the HL7 Gender Harmony gender-identity, pronouns, and recorded-sex-or-gender extensions in the form this reader's profile chooses. Reference-only and ungoverned: no interoperability, clinical, or community reviewer has approved this profile, and validating against it authorizes nothing. It is not a FHIR conformance profile and does not claim conformance with the implementation guide.
$comment: JSON Schema validates structure. The ContextSafe runtime additionally runs the evidence boundary scan before this shape is read, and the observation contract after it; the constraints below are enforced there and cannot be expressed here.
x-contextsafe-semantic-constraints: the source is at most one MiB, is a regular file reached without a final link, and is strict UTF-8 JSON without duplicate keys
no key anywhere normalizes to a prohibited free-text or identifying field (text, contained, note, comment, telecom, address, birthDate, and the rest of the canonical list)

no string carries a boundary-whitespace, control, or format character, a known PHI canary, or a direct-identifier pattern; the five published URLs are exempt from the URL detector by exact equality only
exactly one identifier value equals the case document's synthetic token

which coding shape each sub-extension admits is written below per extension: a gender-identity or pronouns value is a presence coding (the data-absent-reason system with asked-declined, unknown, or not-asked) or a synthetic coding; a recorded-sex-or-gender value is F, M, X, or unknown in any system other than data-absent-reason, because the canonical concept carries no presence state; a recorded-sex-or-gender type is a synthetic coding; the runtime holds the same rule, and checks the recorded-sex-or-gender value against the observation contract's own closed alphabet at the extension's location before conversion

elements admitted here and not carried into the observation set, because the canonical model has no field for them: Patient.id, Patient.active, every HumanName whose use is not usual, family on the usual name, the system of the pronouns coding, and the system of the recorded-sex-or-gender value coding; each is validated and none is free text
a Patient carrying none of the concepts rejects; two gender-identity extensions or two usual names are two observations, which the evaluator reports as ambiguous

codingSystem.description: Bounded at 96 characters, the observation contract's token length, so that a document valid here is not rejected by the contract after conversion.

presenceCoding.description: A presence state: declined, unknown, or not collected. Admissible only where the canonical concept carries a status.

syntheticCoding.description: A synthetic token in any system but the presence system, bounded at 96 characters like the system.

recordedSexOrGenderCoding.description: The observation contract's closed recorded-sex-or-gender alphabet. The concept carries no presence state, so the presence system is not admissible here and its unknown is not this unknown.
